questions.question_text: Which of the following is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Metals such as iron allow heat to pass through them easily, so they are good conductors of heat.

options.option_text: Wood
Iron
Plastic
Rubber

questions.question_text: What happens to mercury in a thermometer when the temperature rises?
questions.explanation: Mercury expands on heating, so it rises up in the narrow tube of the thermometer.

options.option_text: It freezes immediately
It rises in the tube
It changes into gas at once
It becomes shorter

questions.question_text: Heat always flows from:
questions.explanation: Heat moves from a hotter object or region to a colder object or region until the temperatures become more equal.

options.option_text: Cold object to hot object
Hot object to cold object
Heavy object to light object
Bright object to dark object

questions.question_text: Woollen clothes help us stay warm in winter.
questions.explanation: Wool traps air, and air is a poor conductor of heat. This reduces loss of body heat.

options.option_text: True
False

questions.question_text: Which kitchen utensil part is often made of plastic or wood?
questions.explanation: Handles are often made of plastic or wood because these materials are poor conductors of heat and help prevent burns.

options.option_text: The whole pan base
The handle
The flame
The metal spoon bowl

questions.question_text: The SI unit commonly used to measure temperature in science is:
questions.explanation: Temperature is commonly measured in degree Celsius in school science.

options.option_text: Metre
Kilogram
Degree Celsius
Litre

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a poor conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: Wood does not allow heat to pass through easily, so it is a poor conductor.

options.option_text: Copper
Aluminium
Wood
Steel

questions.question_text: Which part of a house is often painted white in hot regions to reduce heating?
questions.explanation: White surfaces reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat, helping keep buildings cooler.

options.option_text: Underground pipes
Roof or outer walls
Door hinges
Water taps

questions.question_text: Transfer of heat through direct contact is called:
questions.explanation: Conduction is the process in which heat passes through a substance by direct contact of particles.

options.option_text: Conduction
Convection
Radiation
Reflection

questions.question_text: Dark-colored clothes usually absorb more heat than light-colored clothes.
questions.explanation: Dark colors absorb more heat energy from sunlight than light colors.

options.option_text: True
False

questions.question_text: Why should we not touch a hot iron rod with bare hands?
questions.explanation: Iron is a good conductor of heat, so the heat quickly travels to the hand and can cause burns.

options.option_text: Because iron becomes lighter when hot
Because iron changes color permanently
Because heat from the rod can quickly reach the hand
Because iron starts absorbing air

questions.question_text: Which clothing is usually more suitable on a sunny summer afternoon?
questions.explanation: Light-colored cotton clothes reflect more heat and allow sweat to evaporate more easily.

options.option_text: Light-colored cotton clothes
Thick black woollen clothes
Wet heavy blankets
Metal-coated clothes

questions.question_text: If steam burns the skin more severely than hot water at the same temperature, what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: Steam carries extra heat energy and can release more heat when it condenses on the skin.

options.option_text: Steam is always colder than water
Steam can transfer more heat to the skin
Water does not contain heat
Steam is not a form of water

questions.question_text: Which observation best shows that metal is a good conductor of heat?
questions.explanation: If one end of a metal spoon in hot soup becomes hot quickly, it shows heat is travelling through the metal.

options.option_text: The spoon floats in water
The other end of the spoon becomes hot soon
The spoon becomes lighter
The spoon changes into liquid

questions.question_text: Why do people use quilts in winter?
questions.explanation: Quilts trap air between their layers. Since air is a poor conductor, body heat escapes more slowly.

options.option_text: Quilts produce heat from nothing
Quilts reduce heat loss by trapping air
Quilts absorb cold from the room
Quilts make the body stop sweating forever

questions.question_text:
Assertion: A metal pan gets heated quickly on a stove.
Reason: Metals are good conductors of heat.
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.option_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true

questions.question_text: Why is it better to wear white clothes than black clothes in summer?
questions.explanation: White clothes reflect more sunlight, so they absorb less heat and help the body stay cooler.

options.option_text: White clothes always produce cold air
White clothes reflect more heat from sunlight
Black clothes are poor conductors
White clothes stop sweating completely

questions.question_text: Name any two good conductors of heat.
questions.explanation: Metals such as copper, iron, and aluminium are good conductors of heat.

questions.question_text: If one end of a wax-coated metal rod is heated and the wax melts farther along the rod, what does this indicate?
questions.explanation: The melting wax shows that heat is travelling through the rod by conduction.

options.option_text: The rod is becoming colder
Wax can move heat better than metal
Heat is spreading through the metal rod
The rod is losing all its mass

questions.question_text: Which statement about temperature and heat is correct?
questions.explanation: Temperature tells how hot or cold an object is, while heat is the energy that flows from hotter to colder objects.

options.option_text: Heat and temperature always mean exactly the same thing
Temperature measures hotness, while heat is energy transfer
Heat is measured only by color
Temperature can move from cold to hot only

questions.question_text: A metal spoon and a wooden spoon are placed in hot water. Which spoon handle will usually feel hotter first, and why?
questions.explanation: Metal conducts heat better than wood, so heat reaches the metal handle more quickly.

options.option_text: The metal spoon handle, because metal conducts heat better
The wooden spoon handle, because wood stores more heat
Both handles always feel equally hot
Neither handle can become hot

questions.question_text: A student wants to compare how fast different materials heat up in sunlight. What is the best next step for a fair test?
questions.explanation: The student should keep the pieces similar in size and place them under the same sunlight for the same amount of time.

options.option_text: Use pieces of very different sizes and colors without notes
Heat one piece in fire and another in sunlight
Keep similar-sized samples under the same sunlight for equal time
Test only one material and guess the others

questions.question_text: In a classroom activity, colored warm water is placed in one corner of a tank of water. The color slowly spreads upward and across. What does this mainly show?
questions.explanation: Warm water rises and cooler water sinks, setting up convection currents in liquids.

options.option_text: Heat travels only through solids
Warm water always becomes heavier
Convection currents are formed in water
Color itself produces heat

questions.question_text: Why does sea breeze usually blow from sea toward land during the daytime?
questions.explanation: Land heats up faster than sea water during the day. Warm air over land rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in to replace it.

options.option_text: Sea water always becomes hotter first
Land heats faster, so cooler sea air moves toward land
Air moves only because of waves
The sea pushes air mechanically toward land

questions.question_text: Why are earthen pots often used for keeping water cool in summer?
questions.explanation: A little water seeps through the tiny pores and evaporates from the outer surface. Evaporation removes heat and cools the water inside.

options.option_text: Earthen pots create cold water by themselves
Clay blocks all movement of heat forever
Evaporation from the pot surface helps cool the water
The pot absorbs only cold from the air

questions.question_text: Which statement correctly describes convection?
questions.explanation: Convection is the transfer of heat by actual movement of particles in liquids and gases.

options.option_text: Convection happens only in solids
Convection happens when warm fluid rises and cooler fluid sinks
Convection needs no particles at all
Convection and reflection are the same thing

questions.question_text: Which pair is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Conduction mainly occurs in solids, while convection mainly occurs in fluids such as liquids and gases.

options.option_text: Conduction - only in empty space
Radiation - only in liquids
Convection - mainly in liquids and gases
Conduction - only in gases

questions.question_text: Why is air trapped between wool fibres useful in winter clothing?
questions.explanation: Air is a poor conductor of heat, so trapped air reduces loss of body heat.

accepted_answers: Air is a poor conductor and slows down heat loss.
Trapped air helps keep body heat from escaping quickly.

questions.question_text: A person stands near a bonfire and feels warm even without touching the fire. Which mode of heat transfer is mainly responsible?
questions.explanation: Heat from the bonfire reaches the person mainly by radiation.

options.option_text: Conduction only
Evaporation only
Radiation
Freezing

questions.question_text: Which observation best supports the idea that black surfaces absorb more heat?
questions.explanation: If two similar containers are left in sunlight and the black one becomes hotter faster, it shows stronger heat absorption.

options.option_text: The white container looks brighter
The black container becomes hotter more quickly in sunlight
The black container is heavier
The white container reflects sound

questions.question_text: If a steel ruler becomes hot at one end and warm at the other after some time, what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: This shows heat is passing through the ruler by conduction.

options.option_text: Heat can travel only through water
The ruler is creating heat at both ends
Heat can move through steel by conduction
The ruler is changing into another material

questions.question_text: Why does hot air usually rise upward?
questions.explanation: On heating, air expands and becomes less dense than the cooler air around it, so it rises.

options.option_text: Hot air becomes heavier
Hot air expands and becomes less dense
Hot air loses all particles
Gravity stops acting on hot air

questions.question_text: You must hold a hot cooking vessel for a few seconds. Which choice is most sensible?
questions.explanation: Using a thick cloth or heat-resistant glove reduces heat transfer to the hand.

options.option_text: Hold it with wet bare fingers
Use a dry thick cloth or heat-resistant glove
Blow on the vessel and grab it immediately
Touch it at the base first

questions.question_text: In an activity, paper spiral hung above a candle begins to rotate. What does this mainly demonstrate?
questions.explanation: The candle heats the air, the warm air rises, and the moving air can turn the spiral. This shows convection in air.

options.option_text: Only conduction in paper
The paper makes wind on its own
Rising warm air due to convection
Candlelight pulls the spiral upward magnetically

questions.question_text:
Assertion: Land breeze generally blows from land toward sea at night.
Reason: At night, land cools faster than sea.
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

options.option_text: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason correctly explains Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason does not explain Assertion
Assertion is true, but Reason is false
Assertion is false, but Reason is true

questions.question_text: Why should a clinical thermometer not be used to measure the temperature of very hot water?
questions.explanation: A clinical thermometer is designed for human body temperature range. Very hot water may damage it or give unsafe results.

options.option_text: Because water has no temperature
Because glass never expands
Because it is made for body temperature range, not very hot liquids
Because hot water always cools before being measured

questions.question_text: A metal bench and a wooden bench are kept outside on a winter morning. Both are at the same surrounding temperature, but the metal bench feels colder. What is the best explanation?
questions.explanation: Metal draws heat away from the body more quickly than wood because metal is a better conductor.

options.option_text: Metal always has a lower temperature than wood
Metal removes heat from the body faster than wood
Wood produces heat for the hand
The color of the bench changes the winter air temperature

questions.question_text: Select all correct statements about radiation.
questions.explanation: Radiation is heat transfer that does not need a material medium and can travel through empty space.

options.option_text: It can occur through empty space
The Sun warms Earth mainly by this process
It happens only in solids
It always requires moving air

questions.question_text: If the windows near the ceiling of a room are opened first, why can the room become cooler more effectively?
questions.explanation: Warm air tends to rise and collect near the top. Opening higher windows lets the warmer air escape first.

options.option_text: Cold air always stays at the top
Windows create new cold air by themselves
Warm air near the top escapes, helping cooler air circulate
Heat cannot move inside rooms

questions.question_text: Which evidence best supports the idea that shiny surfaces are useful in reducing heat absorption?
questions.explanation: If two similar containers are kept in sunlight and the shiny one warms more slowly, it suggests the shiny surface reflects more radiation.

options.option_text: The shiny container is more expensive
The shiny container heats up more slowly under the same sunlight
The dull container is heavier
The shiny container makes louder sound when tapped

questions.question_text: Why are double-walled flasks used to keep liquids hot or cold for a long time?
questions.explanation: They reduce heat transfer by conduction, convection, and radiation, often using vacuum and reflective surfaces.

options.option_text: They add heat to liquids continuously
They change hot liquids into cold ones
They reduce heat transfer in several ways
They absorb all the water inside

questions.question_text: State one difference between conduction and convection.
questions.explanation: Conduction transfers heat without bulk movement of matter, while convection involves movement of particles in liquids or gases.

accepted_answers: Conduction occurs without bulk movement, but convection involves movement of fluid.
Conduction is common in solids, while convection happens in liquids and gases.

questions.question_text: If a black metal can and a shiny metal can are filled with the same hot water, and the black can cools faster, what can be concluded?
questions.explanation: Black surfaces are generally better emitters of heat radiation, so they can lose heat faster.

options.option_text: Black surfaces stop heat transfer
Shiny surfaces always absorb more heat and lose more too
Black surfaces can emit heat faster than shiny surfaces
Color has no relation to heat transfer

questions.question_text: Why does a steel spoon placed in a cup of hot tea become hot even above the tea level?
questions.explanation: Heat travels along the spoon by conduction, so the upper part also becomes hot.

options.option_text: Tea vapour turns the spoon into another metal
Heat conducts through the spoon from the immersed part
Only the air around the spoon heats it
The handle produces heat on its own

questions.question_text: Two students disagree on whether air can transfer heat by convection. What is the most sensible way to test this?
questions.explanation: A simple classroom setup using incense smoke or paper spiral above a warm source can show rising warm air clearly.

options.option_text: Ask only one student to guess
Observe smoke or a paper spiral above a heat source
Put air in a closed book
Use a magnet on the air

questions.question_text: In an experiment, pins fixed with wax on a metal strip fall off one by one when one end is heated. What does this show?
questions.explanation: The falling pins show that heat is moving gradually through the metal strip by conduction.

options.option_text: The wax is attracting the pins upward
The strip is becoming shorter from both ends
Heat is travelling along the metal strip
Metals do not conduct heat at all

questions.question_text: A person wraps a hot casserole in thick insulating material. What is the main benefit?
questions.explanation: The insulating layer slows down the loss of heat from the casserole to the surroundings.

options.option_text: It makes the food cook faster without any heat source
It increases the temperature of the room immediately
It reduces heat loss and helps food stay warm longer
It changes the food into a solid

questions.question_text: Select all correct statements about materials and heat.
questions.explanation: Metals are generally good conductors, while materials like wood, plastic, air, and wool are poor conductors.

options.option_text: Metals are usually good conductors of heat
Air can act as an insulator when trapped
Plastic handles can help prevent burns
All solids conduct heat equally well

questions.question_text: Why is sea water usually cooler than nearby land during the daytime?
questions.explanation: Water heats up more slowly than land, so the sea usually remains cooler during the day.

accepted_answers: Water heats more slowly than land, so sea water stays cooler in daytime.
Land warms faster, while the sea takes longer to heat.

questions.question_text: Why is sweating useful on a hot day?
questions.explanation: When sweat evaporates from the skin, it takes away heat from the body and helps cool it down.

options.option_text: Sweat adds heat to the skin
Sweat prevents all air movement
Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the body
Sweat turns into ice on the skin
